summary: Umpqua NF lookout in Douglas County, Oregon: a 1930 tree platform replaced by an L-4 cab in 1931, gone after 1962-1964.

facts.design: L-4 cab (1931), preceded by a 1930 six-by-six platform built in a tree
facts.status_note: firelookout.com says abandoned in 1964 and gone; the register says removed or destroyed in 1964; Rex's page says dismantled in 1962

staffing.status: a September 1930 newspaper item describes a lookout watching from the tree platform; no later staffing in these sources

events.note: Forest files cited on Rex's page record a one-room log tool house with a shake roof, built for $40
Register: a 6X6 platform built in a tree with a tent nearby; the register's Built field gives 1930
September 1930 Roseburg News-Review item describes the lookout passing many hours each day at the tree platform; no names given
Register and firelookout.com: the platform was replaced by an L-4 cab in 1931; Rex's page lists an L-4 gable roof lookout house built in 1931
Rex's page says the lookout was dismantled in 1962; this conflicts with the 1964 dates on the register and firelookout.com
Register Removed field gives 1964 and says destroyed; firelookout.com says abandoned in 1964 and gone
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites Register November 12, 2019

evidence.supports: site is in the Umpqua National Forest, Douglas County, Oregon
1930 six-by-six platform built in a tree with a tent nearby; replaced by an L-4 cab in 1931; destroyed in 1964
evidence.quote: A 6X6 platform was built in a tree and a tent placed nearby in 1930. This was replaced by a L-4 cab in 1931. The lookout was destroyed in 1964.

evidence.supports: L-4 cab built in 1931, abandoned in 1964, now gone
evidence.quote: Located at the northwest tip below the summit, this L-4 cab, built in 1931, was abandoned in 1964. Gone.

evidence.supports: one-room log tool house built in 1923 per Forest Service files
evidence.quote: 1923: A 6 by 8 log, one room, tool house with a shake roof was constructed at a cost of $40.00.

evidence.supports: September 1930 item: lookout spends many hours each day in a fir top watching for fires
evidence.quote: Chilcoot is a lookout station, and in the top of an adjacent fir the lookout passes many hours each day

evidence.supports: lookout reached by ladder; telephone on the small platform
evidence.quote: Ascent to the lookout is by way of a ladder

evidence.supports: telephone on the small platform links the lookout to the other stations
evidence.quote: is a telephone for transmitting information to all other stations throughout the Umpqua forest

evidence.supports: L-4 gable roof lookout house built in 1931
evidence.quote: 1931: An L-4 gable roof lookout house built.

evidence.supports: Rex's page says the lookout was dismantled in 1962

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Rex's page says the lookout was dismantled in 1962. The register gives 1964 as the removal year and firelookout.com says abandoned in 1964. The story reports the disagreement; the record keeps 1964 from the register and adds the 1962 event.
The register's Built field gives 1930 for the tree platform; the L-4 cab that replaced it is dated 1931 by the register, firelookout.com and Rex's page. Both years are kept as separate events.

sources.title: Chilcoot
sources.publisher: Forest Lookouts (Oregon), Rex's Fire Lookout Page

notes_for_editor: No source describes what remains on the site today, and none gives public access, so access is omitted. The brief's kind 'ground' fits the 1931 L-4 cab, but the 1930 structure was a platform built in a tree, so the editor may want the infobox to show both. Removal year conflicts: the brief's 1964 (from the register) is kept, and Rex's 1962 dismantling is shown as a separate event. The brief's elevation (1519.7 m) matches the register's 4,986 ft. The brief has no height; none is given in the sources, so none is recorded. The register and firelookout.com carry 1940 and 1933 photo credits (Ron Kemnow collection; National Archives Pacific Northwest Region) but no image URLs were pulled, so no photos were added. A web search for Chilcoot Mountain returned only Idaho's Chilcoot Peak, which was excluded.
